extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, astronomers, chemists, and Royal Society readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for observing, recording, comparing, and publishing experimental and observational results (astronomical observations, experimental chemistry/physics, instrument descriptions, and medical case reports). Emphasises reproducibility, instrument specification, controls, and mathematical justification where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility through repeated observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations must be repeated multiple times (over days/years) and shown to agree, even to small units (seconds/minutes), to establish reliability (e.g., distances observed six times in earlier years and re-observed exactly on later dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record multiple independent repetitions of the same measurement; report agreement across repetitions and note any small differences. Anti-pattern: single unreplicated measurements claimed as definitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument comparison by simultaneous observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare different instruments (small/plain sights vs larger/telescopic sights) by making observations contemporaneously to judge relative accuracy and speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have observations performed with both instruments under the same conditions, ideally by the same and by different observers, then tabulate side-by-side results to enable an 'indifferent judge' to assess accuracy. Note observer skill and instrument characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent attestation and witness statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain independent witnesses or attestations from respected observers (e.g., Halley's written attestation) to corroborate the certainty of instruments and observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dated letters or signed attestations from independent parties who observed the work; use their testimony to bolster claims of accuracy. Anti-pattern: relying solely on the author's unsupported assertion of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed recording of dates, methods, and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish full lists of observations with dates, descriptions of methods used, instruments employed, and the success or failure of each observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological logs (dates, N.S. or O.S.), instrument descriptions, exact measured values, and notes on observational conditions. This enables readers to verify, reproduce, or critique the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in responding to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: When criticised, respond publicly with full evidence — observations, correspondence, and methods — to preserve reputation and allow others to judge the dispute (as in publishing letters regarding the controversy over telescopic sights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the underlying data and correspondence that bear on controversies; include rebuttals and the supporting measurements rather than merely rhetorical defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical justification of instrument design choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mathematical analysis for design decisions (e.g., how diagonal divisions on a limb should be spaced and when differences are negligible for large instruments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show computations or refer to prior analyses to justify why a construction is sufficiently accurate; if approximations are used, quantify the expected error and when it can be ignored. Anti-pattern: asserting adequacy without quantitative justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical checks for instrument precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where theoretical differences are predicted (e.g., slight unequal intervals), perform practical checks (e.g., repeating divisions by straight lines from the centre) to demonstrate negligible effect in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine theoretical computation with empirical checking on the actual instrument; document both procedures and their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate map/chart projection and numerical method for intended accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose representations (e.g., using secant sums and a cylinder projection equivalent) and numerical procedures (sums of secants, choice of intervals) that match the intended use and required accuracy of charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain projection rationale (why meridians may be drawn parallel, how to correct latitude/longitude scaling), show trigonometric calculations or series used, and state when simplifications are 'exact enough' for purpose. Provide methods to increase precision (e.g., dividing into parts smaller than minutes or using infinite series) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of infinite series/infinitesimal arithmetic for greater exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: When higher precision is required, apply the arithmetic of infinites and infinite series to obtain quadratures or sums (e.g., for aggregates of secants or tangents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the series expansion and explain truncation rules (when terms can be neglected). Indicate how far to continue series to meet a given tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough listing and description of apparatus and experimental operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical and experimental work, include tables, figures, and detailed operations (e.g., pulverisation of tin, preparation of oils, tinctures, extracts) and any novel manipulations or apparatus designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply drawings/tables of apparatus, step-by-step preparation methods, and notes on reagents and conditions so that others can replicate the procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and isolation of variables in experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Test how specific environmental or procedural changes (air contact, vessel shape, warmth, light) affect phenomena (e.g., motion of a 'self-moving' liquor), to identify causal factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments that isolate single variables (sealed vs open vessels, shallow vs deep containers, warm vs cool settings), record differences systematically, and draw inferences about causes. Anti-pattern: reporting phenomena without attempts to vary and control conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual tracers and simple markers to reveal motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ tracers (bits of straw, detached scum) or visual features (oily patches, coloured halos) to make motions and vortical patterns evident during observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which tracers were used, how they behaved, and what they revealed about flow patterns; include sketches or descriptions of vortical versus progressive motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting observational conditions and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and report observing conditions (light source, day/night, weather, temperature) and the duration over which phenomena persisted (e.g., continued manifest motions over months until vessel upset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit notes about whether observations were by daylight, candlelight, in warm laboratory, etc., and the time span of observations; report when observations ceased and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed structure for medical case reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe patient particulars (name, age, onset and progression), functional status, precise anatomical description of lesions/anomalies (location, appearance, measurements), and how the condition affects daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological history, physical description (texture, colour, size, attachment), and any observed systemic functions; include contextual social details if relevant (care arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe inventions and improvements with operational explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: When introducing or reporting new instruments or improvements (diving bell, air-pump amendments, aerometer, thermoscope), give both constructional details and accounts of experiments demonstrating their function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give schematics or figures, explain how to construct and operate the device, and include experimental results or comparisons showing the improvement's benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical engagement between theory and experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat theoretical claims (e.g., hylarchic principle, elasticity of air) by examining experimental demonstrations and answering arguments; include epistolary exchanges when they clarify points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast theoretical propositions with empirical tests, point out where demonstrations fail or succeed, and publish reasoned replies to opponents with supporting experimental evidence.
